{{Short description|Euclidean solid geometry}}
{{Ref improve|date=February 2024}}
The sweep S<sub>w</sub> of a [[Solid geometry|solid]] S is defined as the solid created when a motion M is applied to a given solid. The solid S should be considered to be a set of points in the [[Euclid]]ean space <math display="inline">\mathbb{R}^3</math>. Then the solid S<sub>w</sub> which is generated by sweeping S over M will contain all the points over which the points of S have moved during the motion M. Solid sweeping which uses this process is employed in different fields, including the modelling of fillets and rounds, interference detection and the simulation of the [[Numerical control|numerical controlled]] machining process.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Hui | first=K. C. | title=Solid sweeping in image space—application in NC simulation | journal=The Visual Computer | volume=10 | issue=6 | year=1994| doi=10.1007/bf01900825 | page=306}}</ref>
